key_insight: ProjectionBench tests whether LLMs can generate scientific hypotheses that stay creative under minimal context and become more grounded as experimental details are progressively disclosed.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark offers a practical way to measure whether AI assistants can support scientific discovery, from early-stage ideation to evidence-aligned reasoning, for future AI scientist systems.
method: Start with only the paper topic and research question.
Reveal technical details in stages and ask the model to generate hypotheses at each step.
Compare generated hypotheses against the paper’s conclusions using automated semantic similarity over atomic claims.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated GPT-5, GPT-5.4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview across 45 papers and reported that GPT-5.4 retained about 0.7 F1 alignment with ground-truth conclusions even under minimal context.
watch_item: Automated semantic similarity may miss subtle scientific nuance, so benchmark scores should be interpreted as a proxy rather than a full measure of discovery quality.
paper_title: ProjectionBench: Evaluating Scientific Hypothesis Generation in LLMs Under Progressive Information Disclosure
